"Create a realistic 3D first-person fishing game set in the middle of the open ocean, on a rusty steel commercial fishing trawler. Use Three.js with a true perspective camera. Mobile-first, but it also works on desktop. Keep the code organized, and store all fish, baits, rods, and upgrades in data arrays so the game generates them automatically. Make sure it builds without errors.
FULL SCREEN
The 3D canvas fills the entire screen (100vw x 100dvh). No header, borders, page scroll, or zoom (touch-action: none, user-select: none).
All UI floats over the 3D view as a small, semi-transparent HUD: coins, current bait, small Shop, Book, and Inventory icons.
CONTROLS
LEFT side: virtual analog joystick for walking forward, backward, and strafing in any direction.
RIGHT side: drag anywhere to look around freely (360 degrees horizontally, about 80 degrees vertically). Full multi-touch so I can move and look at once.
Floating buttons: big Cast/Reel, Pick Up, Bait Select.
Desktop: WASD and mouse.
Smooth acceleration, head bob, and collision with the cabin, railings, and crates so I can't fall off. The camera moves with the rocking boat.
WATER (make this the best part)
Custom ocean shader with layered Gerstner waves (big swells plus small ripples) and animated normal maps.
Fresnel reflections of the sky, sun glitter and glints, deep blue-green depth color, and subsurface glow on wave tops.
White foam on wave crests and around the hull, plus a foam trail and wake behind the boat.
Underwater caustic light patterns, visible depth fog, and fish silhouettes swimming under the surface.
Ripple rings that spread out from the bobber, a splash with droplets when the bobber lands, and bubbles when a fish fights.
Sea spray over the bow, a soft horizon haze that blends the water into the sky, and a gentle swell that rocks the boat.
Weather and time: sunrise, day, sunset, and night with stars and moonlight on the water. Random clouds, light rain, fog, and storms with bigger waves.
BOAT
Detailed trawler with a wheelhouse with windows, metal deck, railings, winch, nets, buoys, crates, barrels, rope coils, a rod rack, a bait station, and a fish cooler. Add rust and weathering, PBR materials, shadows, and tone mapping.
Engine hum, creaking steel, and sound that changes with the weather.
FISHING (must work correctly)
Pick up a rod from the rack. It shows in my hands in first person with a reel.
Hold Cast to charge power, release to throw. The bobber flies in an arc and splashes down based on power.
The fishing line is a real 3D line that updates EVERY frame from the rod tip to the bobber, and later to the hooked fish. It sags slightly and never gets stuck in one spot.
Bite: the bobber twitches and dips, and the phone vibrates. Tap quickly to hook.
Reeling mini-game: tension meter and fight bar. Hold to reel, release to ease off. If tension goes too high, the line snaps. The rod bends and the fish pulls in random directions. Bigger fish fight harder and longer.
The hooked fish is a visible 3D model in the water, thrashing at the end of the line and getting closer as I reel. Big fish leap out of the water.
When it reaches the boat, lift it out and show it hanging in front of the camera for 3 seconds with its name, size, weight, price, and rarity. Then add it to my inventory. Play a special effect for rare and legendary catches.
Fish type depends on bait, depth, time of day, and weather.
200 FISH (generate 3D models from parametric shapes)
Build each fish from a parametric body (length, height, tail shape, fins, color pattern, eyes) so every species looks different. Each fish has: name, rarity, min/max size, weight, price, strength, depth, and favorite bait. There are 100 base species, and each has a rare variant (Golden, Albino, Shadow, or Crystal, with different colors and a glow) for 200 total.
COMMON (20): sardine, anchovy, herring, mackerel, perch, smelt, minnow, sprat, goby, blenny, pilchard, shad, bluegill, sunfish, killifish, silverside, mullet, pinfish, (3D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, mobile-first 3D first-person ocean fishing game in Three.js, with a rusty commercial trawler, detailed ocean effects, fishing mechanics, HUD, and generated fish/tackle data.
- Ensure it works on desktop and mobile, fills the screen, and builds without errors.

## Requirements
- Full-screen, no-scroll/no-zoom canvas; translucent floating HUD.
- Mobile joystick movement, drag-to-look, multitouch, and floating fishing controls; desktop WASD and mouse.
- Realistic ocean, boat, weather/time effects, collision boundaries, and sound effects.
- Functional cast, hook, reel/tension, fish landing, inventory, shop, and field guide.
- Generate 200 fish total from 100 base species and 100 rare variants; keep fish, bait, rods, and upgrades in data arrays.
- Do not ask questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them on completion.

## Decisions
- Created a Vite app using Three.js from npm.
- Chose procedural geometry and custom water shaders rather than external 3D assets.

## Work State

### Completed
- Added project setup in `package.json` and full-screen game shell in `index.html`.
- Added responsive HUD and controls styling in `src/style.css`.
- Added fish, bait, rod, upgrade, and rarity datasets in `src/data.js`.
- Began `src/main.js`: Three.js renderer, ocean shader, trawler/deck details, procedural fish mesh, HUD/modal wiring, fishing interactions, movement, collision, and weather/rain scaffolding.

### Active
- Finish the animation/game loop, dynamic boat sway, cast/reel progression, day/night and storm effects, and startup/resizing behavior in `src/main.js`.
- Install dependencies, run the build, fix errors, and visually inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- `src/main.js` currently ends before the render loop and app initialization, so the game is incomplete and has not been built or tested.

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` from the last edit; finish time-of-day/storm visuals, boat/wake motion, HUD initialization, window resize handler, and animation loop.
2. Check gameplay edge cases, especially bite/hook/reel behavior and duplicate catch handling.
3. Run dependency installation and `npm run build`; fix any errors.
4. Launch the game and inspect a current screenshot; refine visuals/controls and report assumptions and build status.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main Three.js scene and gameplay implementation; unfinished.
- `src/data.js`: Generated species and tackle datasets.
- `src/style.css`: Full-screen responsive HUD and mobile controls.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements.
- `package.json`: Vite scripts and Three.js dependency.

## Important Context
- No build, browser test, or screenshot has been run.
- Changes are uncommitted.

## Objective
- Complete a playable, mobile-first 3D ocean fishing game in Three.js, with a rusty trawler, fishing mechanics, HUD, and generated fish and tackle data.
- Ensure it works on desktop and mobile, fills the screen, and builds without errors.

## Requirements
- Full-screen, no-scroll/no-zoom canvas with translucent HUD; mobile joystick, drag-to-look, multitouch, and floating controls; desktop WASD and mouse.
- Ocean, boat, weather/time effects, collision boundaries, and sound effects.
- Functional casting, hooking, reeling/tension, landing, inventory, shop, and field guide.
- Generate 200 fish from 100 base species and 100 rare variants; keep fish and tackle in data arrays.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking questions; briefly note them on completion.

## Decisions
- Use a Vite app with Three.js from npm and procedural geometry/custom water shaders instead of external 3D assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added project setup, full-screen game shell, responsive HUD/controls styling, and fish/tackle datasets.
- Implemented the Three.js scene, trawler, water shader, fishing interactions, movement/collision, weather scaffolding, and game loop in `src/main.js`.
- Added day/night lighting, boat sway, fish movement, resize handling, and startup/HUD initialization.
- Installed dependencies; `npm run build` succeeds. Vite reports a non-blocking warning that the minified JS chunk exceeds 500 kB.

### Active
- Run the game in a browser, inspect the rendered scene and console, and verify mobile/desktop controls and fishing progression.
- Check gameplay edge cases and wire/verify sound effects.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Open the running app at `http://localhost:3002` with `playwright-cli`; inspect the console and capture/inspect a screenshot.
2. Test rod pickup, cast/bite/hook/reel/landing, HUD/modal interactions, movement, resizing, and mobile controls; fix any issues.
3. Rebuild and report assumptions and verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Three.js scene, gameplay, weather, rendering, controls, and game loop.
- `src/data.js`: Fish, bait, rod, upgrade, and rarity datasets.
- `src/style.css`: Full-screen layout, HUD, and responsive controls.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements.
- `package.json`: Vite scripts and Three.js dependency.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed project files as untracked.
- Browser verification and screenshot inspection have not yet been performed.

## Objective
- Complete and verify a playable, mobile-first 3D ocean fishing game built with Three.js, including an opening view that shows both the trawler deck and ocean.

## Requirements
- Full-screen play with responsive HUD, mobile joystick and drag-to-look, multitouch, and desktop WASD/mouse controls.
- Functional fishing, inventory, shop, field guide, ocean, boat, weather/time effects, collision boundaries, and sound effects.
- Generate 200 fish from 100 base species and 100 rare variants; keep fish and tackle in data arrays.
- Build without errors; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.

## Decisions
- Use Vite, npm Three.js, procedural geometry, and custom water shaders rather than external 3D assets.
- Set the initial camera yaw to `.72` to reveal open water beside the deck.

## Work State
### Completed
- Set up the game shell, responsive HUD/controls, scene, fishing interactions, weather/time scaffolding, sound, and fish/tackle datasets.
- Replaced the tall hull with a low-profile tapered hull.
- Captured the revised opening view; it shows the deck in the foreground and open water to the right.
- Corrected `pickUpRod()` to target the existing `#hint` element after testing exposed a null-element error.

### Active
- Retest rod pickup and gameplay after the `#hint` fix; verify fishing, inventory/shop/field guide, movement, and responsive controls.
- Rebuild and check for runtime errors.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Retest rod pickup after the `#hint` fix and check the browser console.
2. Exercise fishing progression and the HUD/modals, plus desktop and mobile controls and resizing.
3. Run `npm run build` and report verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Three.js scene, camera/hull, gameplay, weather, rendering, and controls.
- `src/data.js`: Fish, bait, rod, upgrade, and rarity datasets.
- `src/style.css`: Full-screen layout, HUD, and responsive controls.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements.
- `screenshots/current.png`: Earlier screenshot, before the latest camera/hull changes.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- The development server responds at `http://localhost:3002`; browser capture is available with `playwright-cli`.
- A browser test exposed `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'style')` in `pickUpRod()` because it referenced `#interaction-hint`; the code now references `#hint`, but this fix has not yet been retested.
- The latest opening screenshot at yaw `.72` showed deck foreground and open water, with the wheelhouse mostly off to the left.

## Objective
- Finish and verify a playable, mobile-first Three.js ocean fishing game, with an opening view that shows the trawler deck and open water.

## Requirements
- Full-screen responsive play with mobile joystick and drag-to-look, multitouch, and desktop WASD/mouse controls.
- Functional fishing, inventory, shop, field guide, ocean, boat, weather/time effects, collision boundaries, and sound effects.
- Generate 200 fish from 100 base species and 100 rare variants; keep fish and tackle in data arrays.
- Build without errors; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.

## Decisions
- Use Vite, npm Three.js, procedural geometry, and custom water shaders rather than external 3D assets.
- Set the initial camera yaw to `.72` to reveal open water beside the deck.

## Work State
### Completed
- Set up the game shell, responsive HUD/controls, scene, fishing interactions, weather/time scaffolding, sound, and fish/tackle datasets.
- Replaced the tall hull with a low-profile tapered hull; opening view shows deck foreground and open water to the right.
- Fixed rod pickup’s missing-element error by targeting `#hint`; browser test confirmed pickup and notice work.
- Tested shop, field guide, inventory, and bait selection; shop lists 10 items.
- Tested casting through a bite and hook; game entered `REEL` phase and showed the hooked fish.
- Confirmed dataset contains 200 fish (100 base, 100 variants), 5 baits, 3 rods, and 3 upgrades.
- Checked 390×844 mobile and 844×390 landscape layouts; document dimensions fit the viewport.
- Added an inline favicon; immediate post-reload console check showed no errors.
- `npm run build` succeeds.

### Active
- Finish gameplay verification through landing a catch, then confirm inventory and field guide update.
- Investigate the mobile joystick synthetic pointer test, which reported no knob movement; verify with real touch-style interaction.
- Check browser console after the joystick probe and assess the large-bundle build warning.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the latest browser console output and verify joystick movement and mobile drag-to-look.
2. Complete a fishing cycle through landing a fish; verify inventory and field guide progression.
3. Re-run `npm run build` after any fixes and report remaining warnings.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Three.js scene, gameplay, fishing, weather, rendering, and controls.
- `src/data.js`: Fish, bait, rod, upgrade, and rarity datasets.
- `src/style.css`: Full-screen layout, HUD, and responsive controls.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM elements, including the inline favicon.
- `screenshots/current.png`: Earlier opening-view capture.
- `screenshots/mobile-test.png`: Mobile viewport capture with the shop open.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- Development server is available at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Build succeeds but Vite warns that the minified JS chunk is about 526 kB, above its 500 kB advisory threshold.
- Rod pickup is fixed and verified; fishing reached the hooked-fish/reel stage, but a catch has not yet been landed or checked in inventory.

## Objective
- Finish and verify a playable, mobile-first Three.js ocean fishing game with an opening view of the trawler deck and open water.

## Requirements
- Responsive fullscreen gameplay with mobile joystick and drag-to-look, multitouch, and desktop WASD/mouse controls.
- Functional fishing, inventory, shop, field guide, ocean, boat, weather/time effects, collision boundaries, and sound effects.
- Generate 200 fish from 100 base species and 100 rare variants; keep fish and tackle in data arrays.
- Build without errors; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.

## Decisions
- Use Vite, npm Three.js, procedural geometry, and custom water shaders rather than external 3D assets.
- Set the initial camera yaw to `.72` to reveal open water beside the deck.

## Work State
### Completed
- Set up the game shell, responsive HUD/controls, scene, fishing interactions, weather/time scaffolding, sound, and fish/tackle datasets.
- Replaced the tall hull with a low-profile tapered hull; opening view shows deck foreground and open water to the right.
- Fixed rod pickup’s missing-element error and wrapped joystick pointer capture in `try/catch` to avoid errors from synthetic pointer events.
- Verified shop, field guide, inventory, and bait selection earlier; shop lists 10 items.

- Added an inline favicon; browser console currently reports 0 errors.
